get.description: Return the template a new Take 5 is filled in on, and its choices.

post.description: Return what is missing, the warnings and the ratings, saving nothing.

Return a nudge for each vague hazard linked to a Yes, saving nothing (T6).

An AI judges the hazards when one is set up, for up to 5 seconds, and the word
rule decides the rest. The phone asks once for each hazard's words.

schema.title: Response Nudges Api Take5S Nudges Post

post.description:
Check and save a Take 5 once, and return it, unfinished, with its question.

A draft with gaps raises `InvalidDraftError`, which `api/errors.py` turns into
a 422.

409.description: This ID was used for other answers

get.description:
Return up to 50 saved Take 5s, newest first, each with its saved verdict.

Args:
    before: The last Take 5 already shown, for the page after it, or None
        for the newest.

post.description:
Save the answer to a Take 5's question, and return it finished.

An answer that is too short raises `InvalidAnswerError`, which
`api/errors.py` turns into a 422.

get.description: Return a saved Take 5 with its verdict, or its question if unfinished.

Rank the Take 5s started since a moment, and find the best (W1 to W9).

Args:
    since: The moment, with its time zone, such as midnight where the phone
        is for "Today's review".

422.description: The moment is missing or has no zone

get.description:
Group the last 30 days of Take 5s by area, hottest first (A1 to A5).

Args:
    today: Midnight today where the phone is, with its time zone.

422.description: The moment is missing or has no zone

Answer.title: Answer
Answer.description: The three answers a question can have. Nothing is picked to begin with.

AnswerRequest.title: AnswerRequest
AnswerRequest.description:
The worker's answer to a Take 5's challenge question.

Attributes:
    answer: What the worker wrote.

AreaRisk.title: AreaRisk
AreaRisk.description:
What the Take 5s in one area show (A3 to A5).

Attributes:
    name: The area, as it was typed most often (A1).
    take5_count: How many Take 5s were done there.
    high_risk_count: How many had a hazard that needed a JHA before controls (A3).
    stopped_count: How many got "Don't start yet". An unfinished one has no
        verdict yet, so it isn't counted.
    thought_gap_count: How many thought gaps they had between them (W2 to W5, W10).
    highest_score: The highest before-controls score of any hazard there.
    highest_band: That score's band, such as "Extreme".
    common_yes: Up to 3 hazard questions answered Yes most often there (A5).

AskedBy.title: AskedBy
AskedBy.description: Who wrote the question the worker was asked.

BestTake5Line.title: BestTake5Line
BestTake5Line.description:
The best careful Take 5 of the set, with what was good about it (spec W8).

Attributes:
    id: The Take 5's ID, to open it.
    created_at: When it was saved.
    worker_name: Who did it. Never sent to the AI.
    job: What the job is.
    can_start: The verdict it was saved with: True for Good to go, False for
        Don't start yet.
    line: One line saying what was good about it.
    picked_by_ai: True when the AI picked it and wrote the line, False when the
        fixed rules did.
    minutes_taken: How many minutes it took, or None when that can't be told.

Challenge.title: Challenge
Challenge.description:
The question a Take 5 was asked, who asked it, and the worker's answer.

Attributes:
    question: The question the worker was shown.
    asked_by: Whether the AI or the fallback asked it.
    model: For an AI question, which model asked it. None for the fallback.
    instructions_version: For an AI question, which version of its instructions
        it had. None for the fallback.
    answer: The worker's answer, or None until they give one.

CommonYes.title: CommonYes
CommonYes.description:
A hazard question answered Yes in an area, and how many times.

Attributes:
    question: The card's question, word for word.
    count: How many of the area's Take 5s answered it Yes.

Control.title: Control
Control.description: What the worker will do about a hazard, and what kind of control it is.

ControlDraft.title: ControlDraft
ControlDraft.description:
A control whose wording or kind may still be missing.

Attributes:
    description: What the worker will do, in their own words.
    kind: The kind of control, or None until one is picked.

enum: Put systems in place (permits, safe work procedures)
ControlKind.title: ControlKind
ControlKind.description: The card's six controls, ordered from strongest to weakest.

DraftCheck.title: DraftCheck
DraftCheck.description:
What checking a draft found.

Attributes:
    errors: Every gap or mistake, in the order of the form.
    warnings: Everything allowed that will stop the job, in the order of the form.
        A warning never stops the draft being submitted.
    assessment: The rated Take 5, or None while there are errors.
    can_submit: True when there are no errors.
    thinking_questions: Applicable prompts, including ones already answered.
    runs_out_at: When the draft runs out (spec K2), or None when it never does.

ErrorMessage.title: ErrorMessage
ErrorMessage.description:
The reply for a 404 or a 409: one message a person can read.

Attributes:
    detail: What went wrong, in plain words.

FieldError.title: FieldError
FieldError.description:
One gap or mistake, and the field it belongs beside.

Attributes:
    path: The field's dotted path, such as `hazards.0.controls.1.kind`.
    message: What to do about it, in plain words.

FieldWarning.title: FieldWarning
FieldWarning.description:
Something allowed that will stop the job, and the field it belongs beside.

Attributes:
    path: The field's dotted path, such as `hazards.0.controls`.
    message: What it will mean, in plain words.

FormErrors.title: FormErrors
FormErrors.description:
The reply for every 422: what is missing or wrong, field by field.

Attributes:
    detail: A summary for the top of the screen.
    errors: Each problem, with the dotted path of the field it belongs beside.

Hazard.title: Hazard
Hazard.description:
One hazard rated before and after controls, using ratings from `rate()`.

Without controls, reuse the before rating as the after rating; no second rating
is needed. Description, ratings and controls are immutable once constructed.
`covers` holds the IDs of the hazard questions answered Yes that the worker linked
to this hazard (T5); it is empty for a Take 5 saved before links were kept.
`kept_flag` is what the hazard check still said about its words when the Take 5
was submitted, so the worker kept them after the nudge (T6, task 0037); None when
nothing was flagged, or for a Take 5 saved before flags were kept.

HazardDraft.title: HazardDraft
HazardDraft.description:
A hazard while the worker is still rating it and writing its controls.

Attributes:
    description: The hazard in the worker's own words.
    before: The rating before controls.
    controls: The controls, possibly none.
    after: The rating after controls. Ignored when there are no controls (R6).
    weak_controls_reason: Why stronger controls aren't possible, when T3 asks.
    covers: The IDs of the hazard questions the worker linked to this hazard (T5),
        whether it was added from a Yes or picked from the list.

HazardFlag.title: HazardFlag
HazardFlag.description: What the hazard check (T6) said was wrong with a hazard's words.

LevelGuidance.title: LevelGuidance
LevelGuidance.description:
What one level of a scale means, in the card's own words.

Attributes:
    level: The level, such as "Rare".
    meaning: What it means, such as "Could happen, but only in rare cases".

Nudge.title: Nudge
Nudge.description:
A suggestion to look again at an answer. It never stops submitting.

Attributes:
    path: The answer's dotted field path, such as `hazards.0.description`.
    message: The suggestion, in plain words.
    question_id: The question to show it under, such as `vehicles`, so the phone
        needn't work out where it goes.
    flag: What is wrong with the hazard's words: vague, stock or unfit.

Question.title: Question
Question.description:
One question on a card.

Attributes:
    id: A short name that stays the same if the wording is tidied, such as
        `permits`. Answers are kept against it. Lower-case letters, digits and
        underscores only, so it is safe in a dotted path like `answers.permits`.
    text: The question as the card prints it.
    role: What its answer means for the job.
    example: For a hazard question, a specific hazard it could be about, shown when
        the worker's own wording is vague. Empty when the card gives none.

QuestionRole.title: QuestionRole
QuestionRole.description: What a question's answer means for the job.

RankedTake5Line.title: RankedTake5Line
RankedTake5Line.description:
One Take 5 in a ranking, worst first, with why it sits there (spec W1 to W7).

Attributes:
    id: The Take 5's ID, to open it.
    created_at: When it was saved.
    worker_name: Who did it (decided by Jake, 2026-11-19). Never sent to the AI.
    job: What the job is.
    can_start: The verdict it was saved with: True for Good to go, False for
        Don't start yet, or None while its question is unanswered.
    line: One line saying why it sits where it does.
    ranked_by_ai: True when the AI placed it and wrote the line, False when the
        fixed rules did.

RankedTake5s.title: RankedTake5s
RankedTake5s.description:
Every Take 5 started since a moment worst first, and the best (W7 to W9, D92).

Attributes:
    take5s: The ranking. The page shows the first 5, then the rest on request.
    best: The best careful one, or None when none is careful.
    typical_minutes: The median minutes a finished one took, or None.

RatingChoice.title: RatingChoice
RatingChoice.description:
A likelihood and a consequence as the worker picked them; neither is preset.

Attributes:
    likelihood: The picked likelihood, or None until one is picked.
    consequence: The picked consequence, or None until one is picked.

RiskByArea.title: RiskByArea
RiskByArea.description:
Every area with a Take 5 in the last 30 days, hottest first (A1 to A5).

Attributes:
    areas: Each area and what its Take 5s show, hottest first.

RiskCell.title: RiskCell
RiskCell.description: One square of a risk matrix: the score it gives and the band that score is in.

RiskMatrix.title: RiskMatrix
RiskMatrix.description:
A risk matrix as data.

Attributes:
    likelihoods: The likelihood scale, most likely first, as printed down the side
        of the card.
    consequences: The consequence scale, least severe first, as printed across the
        top.
    cells: One row per likelihood and, in each row, one cell per consequence, in
        the order of the scales.
    jha_threshold: The lowest score that needs a Job Hazard Analysis (spec R3).

RiskRating.title: RiskRating
RiskRating.description:
A likelihood and consequence, with the score and band the matrix gives them.

The score and band are always looked up, never typed in, so only `rate()` should
make one.

SavedTake5.title: SavedTake5
SavedTake5.description:
A Take 5 as it was saved: what the worker gave, and the verdict they were shown.

It is saved unfinished, before the challenge question is asked (spec C6). The
question is added once, then the answer and the verdict once, and from then on it
is never changed, so it always shows the template and verdict the worker was
given, even after the rules change.

Attributes:
    id: The ID the phone made when the worker started submitting.
    created_at: When it was saved.
    worker_name: Who did the Take 5.
    job: What the job is.
    location: Where the job is.
    finished_at: When the challenge question was answered, or None while it is
        unfinished. A Take 5 saved before task 0008 was finished when it was saved.
    verdict: The verdict the worker was shown, or None while it is unfinished.
    fixes: The ID of the saved Take 5 this one fixes, or None. It points back
        only, so the first Take 5 is never changed when it is fixed.
    started_at: When the worker started it, by the phone's clock, or None for a
        Take 5 saved before task 0019.
    challenge: The question it was asked and the worker's answer, or None until
        it is asked. A Take 5 finished before task 0008 has none.

SubmissionRequest.title: SubmissionRequest
SubmissionRequest.description:
A Take 5 to save, with an ID the phone made so a retry can't save it twice.

Attributes:
    id: Made once by the phone and sent again, unchanged, on every retry.
    draft: The worker's answers.

Take5.title: Take5
Take5.description:
The answers, hazards and template needed to give a Take 5 its verdict.

`SavedTake5` adds the job, the worker and the rest of the completed card. Ratings
must match this template, so a caller cannot supply a different score or band.

Attributes:
    template: The card it was filled in on.
    answers: The answer to each of the template's questions, by question ID.
        Empty for a Take 5 saved before the app asked them, whose template has no
        questions.
    hazards: The rated hazards, at least one.

Take5Draft.title: Take5Draft
Take5Draft.description:
A Take 5 that hasn't been saved, as the phone sends it.

Attributes:
    worker_name: Who is doing the Take 5.
    job: What the job is.
    location: Where the job is.
    answers: The answers picked so far, by question ID. A question with no
        answer is left out.
    hazards: The hazards, in the order the worker listed them.
    fixes: The ID of the saved Take 5 this one fixes, or None for a fresh one.
    started_at: When the worker started it, by the phone's clock, or None if the
        phone didn't say. It must include its time zone.

Take5ListPage.title: Take5ListPage
Take5ListPage.description:
One page of the saved Take 5 list, the newest first (spec D18 and D80).

Attributes:
    take5s: Up to 50 lines of the list.
    next: The ID to send as `before` for the next page, or None when there are no
        more.

Take5Response.title: Take5Response
Take5Response.description:
A saved Take 5, with the overall rating the back end worked out for it.

Attributes:
    take5: The saved Take 5, with its question and a copy of its template. Its
        verdict is empty until the question is answered.
    rating: The Take 5's rating (spec R4 and R5).
    fixed_by: The ID of the newest Take 5 that fixes this one, or None. It is
        found when the Take 5 is opened, because the saved one never changes.
    offers_fix: True when the result should offer to fix this Take 5 in a new
        one: it said Don't start yet and has no fix yet.

Take5Summary.title: Take5Summary
Take5Summary.description:
One line of the saved Take 5 list: enough to find it, not the whole card.

Attributes:
    id: The Take 5's ID, to open it.
    created_at: When it was saved.
    worker_name: Who did it.
    job: What the job is.
    can_start: The verdict it was saved with: True for Good to go, False for
        Don't start yet, or None while its question is unanswered.
    fixed: True when a newer Take 5 fixes this one.

Take5Template.title: Take5Template
Take5Template.description:
The card a Take 5 is filled in on. Each saved Take 5 keeps a copy of it.

Attributes:
    name: The card's name, such as "Take 5 booklet".
    questions: The card's questions, in the order it prints them. Empty for a
        Take 5 saved before the app asked them.
    matrix: The risk matrix the hazards are rated on.
    likelihood_guidance: What each likelihood means, shown beside the rating.
    consequence_guidance: What each consequence means, shown beside the rating.
    control_guidance: What makes a control strong or weak, shown beside the
        controls.
    draft_time_limit_minutes: How long an unfinished Take 5 lasts, counted from
        when it was started (spec K2), or None for no limit, which turns the
        check off completely.
    specific_hazard_words: The fewest words a hazard linked to a Yes can have
        before the worker is asked to make it specific (spec T6), or None, which
        turns the nudge off.

TemplateResponse.title: TemplateResponse
TemplateResponse.description:
The card a new Take 5 is filled in on, so the phone keeps no copy of it.

Attributes:
    name: The template's name.
    questions: The card's questions, in the order it prints them, each with its
        role.
    answer_choices: The answers a question can have, in the order to show them.
    matrix: The risk matrix the hazards are rated on.
    control_kinds: Every kind of control, strongest first.
    likelihood_guidance: What each likelihood means, in the card's words.
    consequence_guidance: What each consequence means, in the card's words.
    control_guidance: The card's advice on choosing controls.
    ai_notice: What Submit sends to the AI, to show above Submit, or None when
        no AI is set up, so nothing is sent (decision D52).
    hazard_ai_notice: That hazards linked to a Yes are checked by an AI, to show
        on the hazard check page, or None when the word rule judges them, so
        nothing is sent (decision D63).

ThinkingQuestion.title: ThinkingQuestion
ThinkingQuestion.description:
A question that applies even once its answer has been filled in.

Attributes:
    path: The answer's dotted field path.
    message: The question to show beside the answer.

Verdict.title: Verdict
Verdict.description:
Whether the job can start, and why not.

Attributes:
    can_start: True for Good to go, False for Don't start yet.
    reasons: Every reason that applies, in the order of the rules (V1, V2, then
        V3).
